This assignment looks at ocean depth and sea surface temperature to calculate the most appropriate zones to cultivate oysters and shrimp. The greater region of study is the Pacifc Coast of the United States, reaching from the Canadian border in the North to the Mexican border in the South. For the shrimp, the most suitable area for cultivation is off the coast of Oregon. For oysters, the most suitable area for cultivation is off the Central Coast of California. 

# Load libraries
```{r}
library(sf)          # vector handling
library(terra)       # raster handling
library(tidyverse)
library(tmap)        # map making
library(elevatr)     # elevation data download
library(tigris)      # US Census boundary data
library(viridisLite)
library(kableExtra) # table formatting
library(spData) # spatial data
library(spDataLarge) # spatial data
library(geodata) # spatial data
library(stars)
```

# Load the data
```{r}
average_sst_2008 <- rast('data/data/average_annual_sst_2008.tif')
average_sst_2009 <- rast('data/data/average_annual_sst_2009.tif')
average_sst_2010 <- rast('data/data/average_annual_sst_2010.tif')
average_sst_2011 <- rast('data/data/average_annual_sst_2011.tif')
average_sst_2012 <- rast('data/data/average_annual_sst_2012.tif')
depth <- rast('data/data/depth.tif')
regions <- st_read('data/data/wc_regions_clean.shp')
```

# Stack the average SST rasters together, calculate the mean, convert to from Kelvin to Celcius
```{r}
average_sst_stack <- c(average_sst_2008, average_sst_2009, average_sst_2010, average_sst_2011, average_sst_2012)
mean_sst <- mean(average_sst_stack, na.rm = TRUE)
average_sst_c <- mean_sst - 273.15
```

# Crop depth raster to the extent of the SST raster, resample to the depth raster. C
```{r}
sst <- ext(-131.9848, -114.9867, 29.99305, 49.98842) 
depth_cropped <- crop(depth, sst)
depth_resampl <- terra::resample(depth_cropped, y = average_sst_c, method = "bilinear")
average_sst_c <- project(average_sst_c, crs(depth_resampl))
```

# Check that the CRSs match
```{r}
cat("\n=== Same CRS? ===\n")
cat("west cost regions vs depth: ", same.crs(regions, depth_resampl), "\n")
cat("west cost regions vs SST stack: ", same.crs(regions, average_sst_c), "\n")
cat("depth vs SST stack: ", same.crs(depth_resampl, average_sst_c), "\n")
```

# Build function to classify ideal regions for aquaculture
```{r}
Species_Regions <- function(minimum_sst,maximum_sst,minimum_depth,maximum_depth,
species_name) {
    rcl_temp <- matrix(c(-Inf, minimum_sst, 0, # not suitable
                    minimum_sst, maximum_sst, 1,  # suitable
                    maximum_sst, Inf, 0), # not suitable
                ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

    # Apply the matrix to reclassify the raster, making all cells 0 or 1 or 2
    temp_rcl <- terra::classify(average_sst_c, rcl = rcl_temp)

    # Define a reclassification matrix for temperature
    rcl_depth <- matrix(c(-Inf, minimum_depth, 0, # not suitable
                    minimum_depth, maximum_depth, 1,  # suitable
                    maximum_depth, Inf, 0), # not suitable
                ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

    # Apply the matrix to reclassify the raster, making all cells 0 or 1 or 2
    depth_rcl <- terra::classify(depth_resampl, rcl = rcl_depth)

    combined <- c(temp_rcl, depth_rcl)

    suitable_zones <- lapp(combined, fun = function(SST,depth) SST * depth)

    regions_rasterise <- rasterize(regions, suitable_zones, field = 'rgn_id')

    suitable_cellsize <- cellSize(suitable_zones, unit = "km", mask = TRUE)

    suitable_zones_mask <- mask(suitable_cellsize, suitable_zones, maskvalues = 0)

    zone <- zonal(suitable_zones_mask, regions_rasterise, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)

    zone_tibble <- as_tibble(zone)

    zone_map <- left_join(regions, zone_tibble, by= 'rgn_id')

    tm_shape(zone_map)+
  tm_basemap('OpenStreetMap')+
  tm_fill(
    fill = 'area', 
    fill.scale = tm_scale(), 
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = 'Suitable Area (km)', 
    position = tm_pos_out('right')))+
    tm_title(species_name)+
    tm_compass(position = c('top', 'right'))
}

```

# Run function on shrimp
```{r}
Species_Regions(minimum_sst = 6, maximum_sst = 12, minimum_depth = -457, maximum_depth = -36, species_name = 'Suitable Areas for Shrimp Development')
```

# Run function on oysters
```{r}
Species_Regions(minimum_sst = 11, maximum_sst = 30, minimum_depth = -70, maximum_depth = 0, species_name = 'Suitable Areas for Oyster Development')
```

# Components of building the function
## Create matrix of ideal temperature, depth for oyster development. Output produces suitable zoenes for oyster development. 
```{r}
rcl_temp <- matrix(c(-Inf, 11, 0, 
                 11, 30, 1, 
                 30, Inf, 0 ), 
                 ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE
                 ) 
sst_rcl <- terra::classify(average_sst_c, rcl = rcl_temp)

rcl_depth <- matrix(c(-Inf, -70, 0, 
                 -70, 0, 1,
                 0, Inf, 0), 
                 ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE
                 ) 
depth_rcl <- terra::classify(depth_resampl, rcl = rcl_depth)

combined <- c(sst_rcl, depth_rcl)

suitable_zones <- lapp(combined, fun = function(SST,depth) SST * depth)
```

### Rasterise the regions, suitable_zones on 'rgn_id'. Calculate ideal cells with masking, summarise and put into a tibble. 
### Join the summarised zones with regions, create the final map. 
```{r}
sf::st_crs(regions) <- terra::crs(suitable_zones)
regions_rasterise <- rasterize(regions, suitable_zones, field = 'rgn_id')
plot(regions_rasterise)

suitable_cellsize <- cellSize(suitable_zones, unit ='km', mask = TRUE)

suitable_zones_mask <- mask(suitable_cellsize, suitable_zones, maskvalues = 0)

plot(suitable_zones_mask)

zone <- zonal(suitable_zones_mask, regions_rasterise, fun = 'sum', na.rm=TRUE)

zone_tibble <- as_tibble(zone)

zone_map <- left_join(regions, zone_tibble, by = 'rgn_id')

tm_shape(zone_map)+
  tm_basemap('OpenStreetMap')+
  tm_fill(
    fill = 'area', 
    fill.scale = tm_scale(), 
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = 'Suitable Area (km)', 
    position = tm_pos_out('right')))+
  tm_title('Suitable Areas for Oyster Development')+
  tm_compass(position = c('top', 'right'))
```
